text:
tess: Quick sync — pulled a new prototype for the Private/VPC setup wizard network step. Need focused feedback on (1) the prerequisite checks flow, (2) inline copy that explains why CIDR choices matter, and (3) keyboard focus order for the troubleshooting panel. Can folks skim?
ben: looking now. my first thought — the checkbox that says 'allow outbound traffic' is ambiguous. is that NAT, or all egress?
maria: good call. suggest changing to 'Allow outbound connections (egress) to Redwood control plane' and add a tooltip: 'Needed for model downloads and telemetry; can be tunneled for on‑prem'.
alex: accessibility quick note: tooltip is fine but make sure it's reachable via keyboard and has aria-describedby on the associated label. Also color contrast on the warning badge is low on mobile.
tess: noted — maria, can you propose a 1‑line tooltip & a 2‑sentence explanation for the troubleshooting drawer? keep it non‑technical.
maria: draft copy: 'Outbound connections let your cluster fetch model updates and send telemetry. If you restrict egress, use our private pull agent or a proxy; see docs for proxy examples.' For drawer intro: 'If connectivity checks fail, try these steps in order — they are safe to run and won't change your network config.'
sam: re: troubleshooting order — we should surface quick, reversible checks first: DNS, control‑plane ping, firewall port list. then advanced: routing table / BGP. customers hate seeing advanced stuff upfront.
ben: implementation note — current preflight runs all checks serially which adds 10–12s. Could we parallelize dns+ping and show progressive badges?
tess: parallelizing would help UX. if backend can't do it in time, we can fake progressive updates client‑side for now — show 'running' states and surface results as they come back.
alex: keyboard flow: when drawer opens, focus should move to first actionable item and trap until closed. Close button must be labeled 'Close troubleshooting steps' for screen readers.
maria: copy tweak — instead of 'CIDR' use 'IP range (CIDR)', with a tooltip: 'CIDR is a compact way to describe IP ranges, e.g., 10.0.0.0/16'. avoids jargon.
bot: deploy-bot: screenshot updated at https://assets.redwood.ai/prototypes/private-wizard/v3.png
ben: seeing screenshot — I like the compact checklist, but the progress dots at top feel redundant with per-check status. consider dropping dots and using only per-check badges (success/warn/error).
tess: agree re: dots. Also want to keep a persistent 'contact support' link visible when any check fails — not buried in drawer.
sam: small product ask: add an opt‑out for telemetry in the preflight modal. enterprise customers sometimes require explicit opt‑out during private install.
maria: proposed microcopy for failed DNS: 'Hostname resolution failed. Check your DNS servers or add an entry for control.redwood.internal. Tip: try `nslookup control.redwood.internal` from your bastion.' Should we include the inline code sample?
alex: code is okay but wrap as a <code> and ensure high contrast background for code block. Also ensure copy isn't prescriptive for network admins — phrase as suggestion.
ben: backend side — we can include a 'run this command' button that opens a modal with the command pre‑populated. dangerous? need a confirmation and explicit label 'Copy command to clipboard' only — not run.
tess: yes, copy only. good safety rule.
maria: accessibility and copy together: change 'Run diagnostics' button to 'View diagnostics steps' — clearer and less scary.
ben: minor UI nit — the success badge color is our regular green, but under high contrast themes it blends. pick a slightly darker shade or add an icon.
alex: add icons + text, don't rely on color alone.
sam: logging ask: make the checklist exportable as a plain text summary for support tickets. small UX: 'Export diagnostic summary' button next to 'Contact support'.
tess: prioritize: 1) copy swaps (CIDR -> IP range (CIDR), Run -> View), 2) tooltip text + keyboard/aria fixes, 3) replace progress dots with per‑check badges, 4) add export button + support link, 5) parallelize checks if possible.
maria: I'll push a design update with copy changes and a high contrast set.
ben: I'll scope parallelization and the copy‑only 'copy command' modal.
alex: I'll write a checklist for ARIA attributes and focus behavior.
sam: I'll add telemetry opt‑out and export summary to the requirements doc.
tess: awesome — can we aim for a follow‑up sync Friday EOD? drop comments inline on the prototype in Figma first. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
